description: Runs the project's gdUnit4 tests headless and answers with every case that did not pass: where it is, and what the assertion said. Each entry under failed carries its first report as message and detail, and, when it has more than one, its reports under reports in the order the case met them: gdUnit4 goes on past a failed assertion, and a case can fail several and then stop on a runtime error, which makes its status error. Identical reports fold into one with times, at most twenty different ones are kept (reportsLeftOut counts the rest), and past about a megabyte the largest cases keep only their first message (failedWithoutDetail). failures counts the cases that failed an assertion and errors the cases that hit an error, so such a case counts in both. Suites where everything passed are counted, not listed, and an engine message keeps the frames above gdUnit4, not the twenty inside it; identical engine messages come back once under engineEntries, with times saying how often they were printed, and engineErrors counts every one. The class list is rebuilt first, so a suite written a moment ago is found, and the rebuild's answer is under classes, with the classes each addon declares counted under addedInAddons and changedInAddons rather than named: a class it puts back that the cache had after the last rebuild is named under classes.lostSinceLastRebuild, which is the editor writing its shorter list over the file on every save until restarted. What changed on disk since it was imported is then imported before any suite runs, and named under importedFirst. On Windows and Linux the run gets a user:// of its own, away from a player's saves; on macOS the engine reads user:// off HOME, so it writes where the player keeps theirs, and savesNote says so. A run that found nothing to run is never called a pass, and names the path it looked in. A script that does not load stops gdUnit4 before any suite runs: its errors come back in full under scriptErrors, and the scripts that failed only because one they depend on did are listed by path under failedThroughDependency. When they failed on a class whose own script has a parser error, which gdUnit4 never names, that script is checked by the engine and its error comes first under scriptErrors, with the class it declares under declares, and the errors a script has only because that class did not resolve, which the engine reads as Variant, are kept apart under followFromUnresolved. An autoload that does not compile stops the run at once, its errors listed the same way. A client sending a progress token is told as each suite finishes, and at least every twenty seconds. A run that ends without a report, at its timeout or otherwise, names the suites it finished under suitesFinished, the failing ones with their failed cases under suitesFailing, and the one it was in under suiteRunning. When a client cuts a run off, that is kept in the project and the next project_test there carries it under previousRunCut. A run where nothing failed but nodes were left in the tree comes back under warnings, with the count per suite: gdUnit4 decides its verdict on those and keeps them out of its report, so they are read off what it printed. A run whose every case passed is still not called passed when it printed a script error that no case failed on: gdUnit4 fails a case on the script errors its logger sees, and it cannot see a stack overflow, so the cases pass on whatever the faulted calls returned. Those errors come back under uncaughtScriptErrors, and under engineEntries by index with detailUnder rather than with their backtrace a second time; a backtrace that repeats, as a recursion's does, has each repeated frame or cycle of frames written once with the frames it covers and how many times. One raised inside assert_error(...).is_runtime_error is the test's own and does not count, and none count when the project turns off gdUnit4's report/godot/script_error setting. Needs gdUnit4 under addons/gdUnit4. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

engineArgs.description: The engine's own flags for the run, such as ["--verbose"], a value going as the next entry. Only those that change what the engine logs, draws for debugging, checks on the GPU, which renderer draws, how it times frames or whether it builds the tree a screen reader reads: --verbose, --quiet, --debug-collisions, --debug-paths, --debug-navigation, --debug-avoidance, --debug-stringnames, --debug-canvas-item-redraw, --debug-mute-audio, --print-fps, --gpu-profile, --gpu-validation, --gpu-abort, --disable-vsync, --frame-delay, --time-scale, --fixed-fps, --max-fps, --resolution, --write-movie, --rendering-driver, --rendering-method, --accessibility. Any other is refused. With --verbose, engineEntries holds the ordinary lines the run printed as well, which is where the engine names the instances leaked and the resources still in use at exit.

failFast.description: Stop each suite at its first failing case. Default false: every case runs. With it on, the counts are of what ran, notRun says how many cases were left, and fixing what is named and running again finds the next one, which looks like a flaky tier and is not.

ignore.description: Suites or cases to leave out, as "suite_name" or "suite_name:test_name". A bare test name is read as a suite name and leaves out nothing; an entry that named a case which ran all the same comes back under ignoreNotApplied with the form that would have left it out.

path.description: A test directory or suite file inside the project, or a list of them, all run on one engine: a named set of suites boots once rather than once per suite. An entry given twice, or a suite inside a directory also listed, runs once. An entry that is not there is left out and named under missing, the rest run, and such a run is never called passed; when no entry is there the run is refused before the engine starts, naming each one. Default test.

printed.description: Also answer with every line the run printed that contains this, under printed, whether it passed or not: a suite that prints a marker beside the numbers it measured carries them back without failing an assertion to do it. Matched case aside, in the text and the backtrace, at most 200 lines, the newest kept; printedOmitted counts the rest.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

tests.description: Run only these cases of the suites under path, each "test_name" or "suite_name:test_name", the suite by its file name without .gd or its res:// path. Only the suites holding them run, with their other cases left out. A name no suite there declares as a top-level func is refused before the engine starts, with the nearest names; a case asked for that gdUnit4 did not report comes back under testsNotRun, and the run is not called passed.

timeoutMs.description: How long the run may take before it is killed. Default 600000. A run killed at the limit answers timedOut and silentForMs, how long it had printed nothing; it is called hung only when that was half the limit, or thirty seconds of a longer one, and otherwise it was still running and wants a longer timeoutMs or a narrower path, unless it ended repeating one script error, which the verdict names instead. A run whose autoload did not compile is stopped as soon as the engine says so, and names the script that did not under scriptErrors.

name: project_test
title: Run tests
